Subject: Intermittent packet blackouts over Equinix cross-connect — suspected SNAT/ACL/MTU

Hi Aditya / team,

We're seeing short (~30s) blackouts from our on-prem cluster to Redwood's private endpoint across the Equinix cross-connect; the pattern is roughly every 20-30 minutes and affects ~10% of flows. No CPU spikes on the app nodes, but clients report connection resets and HTTP 504s.

What we've collected so far: tcpdump from a server during an incident, traceroutes from our edge, and a list of recent network changes (none on our side in the last 48 hours). Attaching the pcap and traceroutes.

Observed symptoms:
- Some flows appear to stop mid-transfer then resume after ~20-40s.
- When it happens we see repeated SYN retries on the server side and duplicate ACK bursts.
- Fragmented packets observed in the tcpdump, and some ICMP "fragmentation needed" responses.

Can Redwood confirm whether the cross-connect or your edge is applying any source NAT, ACLs, or doing MTU clamping? Also let us know if you want packet captures from your edge or BGP adjacencies.

Thanks,
Liam
Liam O'Connor
NetOps Lead, Acme Payment Systems

Liam — thanks for the fast heads up and the captures. We're triaging this now. A couple quick asks so we can narrow root cause:

1) Can you confirm whether your cross-connect is advertised as a /31 or /30 on your side and share the BGP peer config?
2) Any recent change to MTU on your colo ports or top-of-rack switches?
3) If you have flow logs from the border router for the timeframe, please include them.

From our side, we'll check:
- Whether the Equinix port on our side has toggled jumbo frames or if there's any SNAT applied at an overlay/edge appliance.
- Security group rules in front of the private endpoint and any recent firewall policy changes.
- We'll run tcpdump at our edge and share before/after captures.

Rishi / Mina — can you pick this up? Rishi, please review session tracking and conntrack timeouts for the private endpoint pool. Mina, please validate SGs and confirm no recent changes in our infra.

I'll schedule a short bridge if needed but want to collect the items above first.

— Aditya

Quick internal notes:
- I'll collect conntrack stats and token bucket drops from the NAT instances serving Acme's pool. If we have asymmetric routing causing replies to traverse a different edge, that could explain the SYN/duplicates.
- Action: I'll run a short tcpdump on pair of production nodes bound to Acme's VIPs for 30 minutes and share.

Mina — can you confirm the security group attached to the private endpoint (svc-acme-vip) and whether there were any ACL updates in the last 72h? If the edge is fragmenting or dropping fragments (ACL rule drop for fragmented traffic) we need to know.

Also proposing: check PMTU from our endpoint to the first hop on Acme side; if MTU mismatch is present we'll see ICMP PMTUD messages in the capture.

— Rishi
From: Natalie Stoques <natalie.stoques@equinix.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@acme-payments.com>
Cc: netops@acme-payments.com
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:22:00 -05:00
Subject: RE: Intermittent packet blackouts over Equinix cross-connect — suspected SNAT/ACL/MTU

Hi everyone — Equinix engineering has completed a preliminary review of the port and cross-connect path for the timestamps you provided. Findings: 

1) We observed a port-level translation on the tenant-facing appliance for the specific cross-connect session: a selective source rewrite was enabled as part of a legacy troubleshooting profile applied to the physical port (this is not a global SNAT but a port profile that rewrites source for certain ephemeral flows).
2) MTU on the Equinix port was set to 1500; however, our internal fabric neighbors were handling some jumbo frames (9000) from a nearby tenant due to mixed MTU on the leaf — leading to fragmentation and intermittent ICMP "fragmentation needed" messages propagating into the path.
3) An ACL on the physical port was configured to drop fragmented packets (we have an old 'drop-fragment' policy that was inadvertently applied when the port was cloned). That matches the captures showing fragments and ICMP PMTU.

We've attached the port configuration snapshot and our view of the traceroute during an incident. Recommended immediate mitigations:
- Remove the legacy 'source-rewrite' profile from the port (we can schedule a short maintenance to do that).
- Disable the 'drop-fragment' ACL for the port to allow path MTU discovery, and coordinate MTU normalization across the leaf fabric.
- After changes, run simultaneous tcpdump on both sides for a 30-minute window to validate.

We're available for a maintenance window today 13:00-14:00 ET or tomorrow morning. If you want us to apply the changes, please confirm and we'll open a maintenance ticket.

Attachments: equinix-port-config-20261110.txt

— Natalie Stoques
Equinix Customer Engineering

1) We'll approve Equinix's maintenance for today 13:00-13:15 ET to remove the 'source-rewrite' port profile and temporarily disable the 'drop-fragment' ACL.
2) Rishi will capture tcpdump on our egress edge; Liam please capture simultaneously on Acme's side. We'll meet back at 13:30 for validation.
3) If metrics look healthy, we'll schedule a follow-up for MTU normalization across the leaf fabric and an RFC to prevent port-profile cloning from applying legacy policies.

Jonas — can you own the post-change audit (route tables, conntrack sweep, and SG validation) and file NET-4321 with the remediation steps?
